questions.q: According to Seneca, what makes a long life seem short?
a: Chasing leisure, luxury and legacy
Working too many hours each week
Failing to plan for retirement
Spending too little time with family
questions.why: Lesson 1 names leisure, luxury and legacy as the pursuits that make life seem shorter than it is.

questions.q: What question does the summary suggest asking to judge an activity's worth?
a: What would this amount to if I did it for 24 hours straight
Would this impress the people whose opinions I admire
Will this still matter a hundred years from now
How much money could this activity earn me
questions.why: Lesson 1 suggests asking what an activity would amount to if you did it for 24 hours straight.

questions.q: What does Seneca's ship metaphor illustrate?
a: A long voyage is about direction, not just time at sea
Safety lies in staying in the harbor
Good weather matters more than the route
Retirement is the safest port after a career
questions.why: Lesson 2 uses the ship metaphor to argue that a long life is about direction, not just time spent.

questions.q: According to Seneca, what can no one take from you?
a: The ability to contemplate life and appreciate its beauty
The wealth you have earned through hard work
The legacy you leave behind after death
The years you have already spent wisely
questions.why: Lesson 3 says no one can take your ability to contemplate life or to appreciate its beauty.

questions.q: What does Seneca say about being busy?
a: You can stay busy your whole life without doing anything meaningful
Busyness is the surest sign of a productive life
Only busy people can truly appreciate leisure
Busy people make the best use of their time
questions.why: Lesson 2 warns that constant busyness is not the same as living a life of real value.
